summary: ```markdown # Animation Production - Animation Optimization p03: Some Considerations ## Introduction Hello everyone, let's take a look at some of the problems that need to be avoided in the process of recording animation in software. ## Importing OBJ for Morph Target Here we import an OBJ to do morph target. After opening it in the right position, we select "Open" at the bottom. Select "Morph Target" for the target type. The morph target is the number of times we have overacted. The smaller the number, the less the number of times we have overacted. The faster we overact, the faster we overact. ### Setting Morph Target So when we set the morph target, try to set it a little higher. This can prevent some cross-interference problems caused by overacting too fast. Also, in the process of morph target, if the movement is too different, such as turning around or encountering other problems, it is best to turn your model in the software first, then do the morph target. Don't make too much of a difference. ## Model Stability Next, we can see that after we have finished the movement, the model's right hand is more stable. However, if we turn to the left hand of the model, we will find that it is a little unstable. The reason why it is unstable is because of the cross-interference between the model's hand and chest. ### Cross-Interference Issues When there is cross-interference in the model, there is also cross-interference in the model's outer panel, because the distance between them is very close. The fabric itself is relatively thin, and the tight position may be fine, but in places where there is more fabric piled up, its instability will be more obvious due to the presence of many grids. Plus, their collision distance now becomes very close, making it easy to cause instability. ### Fixing Instability In such a situation, it may be easier to solve some more tight panels. You can fix it directly through the fixing needle and force it to be fixed in that position. However, if there is a lot of fabric, there is no way to use the function of fixing it to the virtual model. In general, we recommend that you try not to let the movement have some cross-interference. Once cross-interference occurs, it separates the movement from the fabric itself, which also has a calculation impact. ## Animation Recording Considerations Before the official recording starts, ensure your model is in the process of animation recording. Otherwise, there may be cross-interference during the animation recording. ### Ground Conflicts Next, let's look at the second case. In this case, after opening the animation editor, when dragging the progress bar at the bottom, this model may pass through the ground. In our software, there will be conflicts with the ground under default conditions to prevent the panel from falling below the ground. ### Setting Ground Conflicts In this case, if we continue to maintain the conflicts on the ground, then the panel will definitely be forced above the ground, causing the clothing to look like there is a breakdown. We need to set up the conflicts on the ground. In the background of the 3D space, right-click and select the model attribute. Open the ground in the attribute editor. The ground is randomly selected conflicts. When you select a conflict, we can set its overall ground height to negative, placing the position of the conflict below the ground. You can do a test in advance using a piece of board to simulate and see its final height. ## Name Line Details Next, let's look at another case. In this case, I have done some details of the clothes in advance, including using the name line. However, the name line I used is all sticked. First, we can switch to the top stitch, which is the window of the name line. Click the title name here in the bottom window and switch to top stitch. ### Name Line Type Settings When we select a top stitch, which is the type of the name line, in the attribute editor, there is a name line of this type with its attribute settings. Here we will see that there is a type at the bottom with two options: one is OBJ and the other is texture. When we change the type to OBJ, we can see that the details of the name line here will be richer. However, this will lead to certain problems. When we make a mirror, the problem may occur because the number of its grid is large. When you export the LAMBEC file, these name line grids will be animated along with the version, causing the whole project file to become very large and potentially problematic during export. Therefore, in the process of making animations, it is advisable to convert these name lines into texture. ## Costume Changes During Animation Next, let's take a look at the process of recording the animation. Sometimes we may need to make changes to the costume. In the process of making some changes, you need to avoid certain problems. Sometimes, when we start recording the animation, we may not notice any issues. However, after recording the animation to a certain number of frames, we might find differences or unstable places in the version. ### Issues with Animation Frames Some friends may change the costume under the recorded number of frames, and you will find that if you add some false frames or edit the version, the animation recorded before will be gone. This is because our animation moves along the grid. If you change the costume due to the lack of the costume animation, when we drag the progress bar back to the first frame, the previous action and clothes will not match. ### Recommended Steps If you accidentally encounter such a problem, please pause the simulation and save the current action of this OBJ model. After the first frame, you can start to edit your costume. This means that we need to start recording the animation again from the beginning. In addition to the false frame that can cause the recorded animation to fail, if you change the grid peak and perform other operations, there may be animation loss. ## Common Operations and Their Effects Next, let's take a look at what common operations can be done. First of all, these functions will usually cause the grid to reset, including modifying the board, modifying the line, adjusting the particle diameter, increasing the false frame, and adjusting the rendering thickness. Note that this is to adjust the rendering thickness rather than the collision thickness, as the collision thickness is simply the air wall setting, while the rendering thickness can be adjusted. ### Layer Settings The next question is about our layer settings. Before you record the animation, you may use some layers, such as adding a multiple layer to the top layer, so it can be received in the skirt. These settings can be maintained in a static state, but there may be some problems under the dynamic model. ### Identifying Layer Problems In the process of modifying to half, there may be conflict problems. You can see that there are issues in our sleeves or belt. This is because when the animation simulates to this action, the sleeves and skirt collide, leading to layer identification. Initially, it may not touch each other, but if there are collisions during the simulation, we can cancel the layer before it collides. ### Adjusting Layers The layer tool allows you to simulate stability. If there is no problem, we can pull the progress bar back a little and set the layer to zero, then continue to record the animation. The layer will not affect the grid arrangement, so if we start recording the animation, it will not disappear. ## Conclusion Here, I have already recorded a section. Now let's show this section to see if the layer is not applied, what will happen if we start recording. We can observe that if we do not set the layer, it may be more stable. Therefore, whether recording an animation or creating a static model, we should check if the layer is set to prevent issues. Of course, sometimes it doesn't matter if you use the layer; it depends on whether the second time and other versions have collisions. ### Final Thoughts Then let's look at some settings about the animation part. The animation bar is only set to three, but they will merge into a complete animation. The parts that are covered and recorded will not be retained; it will only retain the part that we replaced later. If you don't want to keep those animations recorded later, you can delete them with the right-click option. In addition, when some clothes are hidden when they are leaked, for example, if I choose the skirt and press Shift-Q to hide it, the skirt part will not be leaked when I choose to leak the Olympic file. Here we can see that only the animation above has been leaked. Thank you for watching. ```
